text:
alex: Quick heads-up — testing latency-based region selection + model-variant fallback for hosted customers. Seeing requests flip between eu-west and us-central during burst scale-down, and sometimes we fallback to the 4-bit quantized variant which causes extra routing churn.
maria: hmm — are the probe windows too short? if health probes flip fast, the router will bounce. how long is your probe TTL?
alex: current probe interval 5s, ttl 10s. routing policy: prefer region by median p50, fallback to next region or quantized model when latency > 200ms. customer tier: gold pinned to eu unless > 500ms.
jon: 5s probes is aggressive for noisy networks. add hysteresis: require 3 consecutive failing probes before switching region, and a cooldown of 60s after a fallback.
tara: +1 on hysteresis. also consider treating "variant fallback" differently from region failover — falling back to quantized model should not immediately trigger cross-region failover.
alex: good point. right now those are coupled: any fallback increments region penalty score.
sam: can we split the penalty buckets? one for region-health, one for model-quality. region-health should be probe-based, model-quality driven by token-error-rate or latency regressions.
maria: propose config snippet (pseudo-yaml):

```
routing:
  probe_interval: 10s
  probe_consecutive_failures: 3
  fallback_cooldown: 60s
  penalties:
    region: 1.0
    model_variant: 0.2
  model_variant_policy:
    allow_fallback: true
    degrade_only_for_latency: true
```

jon: also add smoothing for observed latency distribution: use exponential moving average on p50 with alpha=0.2 so short spikes don't flip region.
tara: console UX note — ops folks want to see a timeline that separates region switches vs variant fallbacks in the rollout view. currently the graph overlays both and it's confusing.
alex: yep, saw that in the canary last night. dashboard sank to red but it was just model quantization stepping in. ops escalated unnecessarily.
infra-bot: rollout/17823: canary deployed to eu-west (5%) — health ok :white_check_mark:
sam: idea — an explicit "safety fence" for customer tiers: gold customers get a stricter cooldown and higher penalty for region change, while dev accounts keep aggressive latency-first routing.
maria: agree. defaults: {gold: cooldown 120s, penalty region 2.0}, {standard: cooldown 60s, penalty 1.0}
jon: we should add a circuit-breaker metric: "region_switch_rate" per minute. if > X, suspend automated region routing for that tenant and open a manual ticket.
tara: for console: add a small inline control on route config to toggle "treat model_variant as soft fallback" vs "hard failover".
alex: i'll prototype the routing changes and update the rollout UI ticket. can someone own a short experiment plan?
maria: i'll take the experiment plan. i'll include metrics: region_switch_rate, variant_fallback_rate, p50 by region, error-rate post-fallback.
sam: i'll help with alert thresholds and tenant overrides.
jon: i'll add the EMA smoothing + probe changes in the router shim.
alex: thanks all. assigning follow-ups: jon (router code), maria (experiment + dashboard panels), sam (alerts + tenant defaults), tara (console control UX). i'll post a short status update after first run.

alex: FYI — logs that showed flipping (snippet):
```
[2026-02-03T21:12:02Z] req=abc123 tenant=acme region=eu-west p50=210ms -> fallback model=v4q
[2026-02-03T21:12:07Z] probe eu-west failed (1/3)
[2026-02-03T21:12:09Z] region penalty eu-west += 1.0 (now 1.8)
[2026-02-03T21:12:11Z] router selected us-central for tenant=acme
```

maria: perfect, helps debug. small nit: include whether the fallback was auto or policy-driven.
jon: noted. i'll emit extra fields in router logs.
alex: cool — we'll regroup after first experiment run. :thumbsup:
